item.research_question: How can single-atom ruthenium catalysts be engineered to achieve high activity and stability for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), and what is the dynamic structural evolution of the active site under working conditions?
item.material_system: Single-atomic Ru anchored on nitrogen-carbon support (Ru1-N4 configuration), specifically Ru-N-C derived from phosphide carbon nitride with 1.0 wt.% Ru loading
item.processing_route: Wetness impregnation of RuCl3 precursor into phosphide carbon nitride dispersion followed by pyrolysis at 300 °C for 2 h in argon atmosphere; precursor preparation involved pyrolysis of urea at 600 °C and phosphorization at 300 °C
item.test_conditions: O2-saturated 0.5 m H2SO4 electrolyte; linear sweep voltammetry (5 mV s−1) from 1.1–2.0 V vs. RHE; chronoamperometry at 1.5 V vs. RHE for 30 hours; operando SR-FTIR and XAFS at 1.5 V vs. RHE
key_findings: Achieved a low overpotential of 267 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2
Delivered a mass activity of 3571 A gmetal−1 and a turnover frequency (TOF) of 3348 O2 h−1 at 267 mV
Showed only ~5% degradation and 5% Ru dissolution after 30-hour operation in acidic environment
Operando SR-FTIR identified a new absorption band at ~764 cm−1 appearing at 1.5–1.6 V vs. RHE, assigned to single oxygen adsorption
Operando XAFS revealed a 0.07 Å low-R shift in the first coordination peak and a shortened Ru-N/O bond length of 2.05 Å under working conditions
Theoretical calculations determined the overpotential for the O-Ru1-N4 configuration is 0.59 V, significantly lower than the 0.83 V for ex situ Ru1-N4
The catalyst exhibited a Tafel slope of 52.6 mV dec−1 and interfacial charge-transfer resistance of 178 Ω
item.mechanism: Under working potentials, a single oxygen atom dynamically adsorbs onto the Ru1-N4 site to form an O-Ru1-N4 configuration; this adsorption induces structural relaxation (shortening of Ru-N bonds) and electronic changes (increased electron transfer from Ru 4d to N 2p and O), optimizing the binding energy of oxygen intermediates and lowering the energy barrier for the O-O coupling step (formation of OOH*), thereby enhancing activity and stability by preventing lattice oxygen evolution and Ru dissolution.
item.limitations: Theoretical overpotential values are slightly higher than experimental values due to the use of simplified models in the DFT calculations
item.future_work: The discovery of structural evolution under working conditions provides a coordination-engineered strategy for designing high-performance acidic OER electrocatalysts for future PEMWE applications
quotes: The single-atom Ru-N-C catalyst delivers an exceptionally intrinsic activity, reaching a mass activity as high as 3571 A gmetal−1 and turnover frequency of 3348 O2 h−1 with a low overpotential of 267 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2.
Operando synchrotron radiation X-ray absorption spectroscopy and infrared spectroscopy identify the dynamic adsorption of single oxygen atom on Ru site under working potentials.
Theoretical calculations validate that such O-Ru1-N4 site possesses an optimized binding energy of oxygenated intermediates, and thus boosting OER activity.

records.text: Paper card. Question: How can single-atom ruthenium catalysts be engineered to achieve high activity and stability for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), and what is the dynamic structural evolution of the active site under working conditions?. System: Single-atomic Ru anchored on nitrogen-carbon support (Ru1-N4 configuration), specifically Ru-N-C derived from phosphide carbon nitride with 1.0 wt.% Ru loading. Processing: Wetness impregnation of RuCl3 precursor into phosphide carbon nitride dispersion followed by pyrolysis at 300 °C for 2 h in argon atmosphere; precursor preparation involved pyrolysis of urea at 600 °C and phosphorization at 300 °C. Test conditions: O2-saturated 0.5 m H2SO4 electrolyte; linear sweep voltammetry (5 mV s−1) from 1.1–2.0 V vs. RHE; chronoamperometry at 1.5 V vs. RHE for 30 hours; operando SR-FTIR and XAFS at 1.5 V vs. RHE. Findings: Achieved a low overpotential of 267 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2; Delivered a mass activity of 3571 A gmetal−1 and a turnover frequency (TOF) of 3348 O2 h−1 at 267 mV; Showed only ~5% degradation and 5% Ru dissolution after 30-hour operation in acidic environment; Operando SR-FTIR identified a new absorption band at ~764 cm−1 appearing at 1.5–1.6 V vs. RHE, assigned to single oxygen adsorption; Operando XAFS revealed a 0.07 Å low-R shift in the first coordination peak and a shortened Ru-N/O bond length of 2.05 Å under working conditions; Theoretical calculations determined the overpotential for the O-Ru1-N4 configuration is 0.59 V, significantly lower than the 0.83 V for ex situ Ru1-N4; The catalyst exhibited a Tafel slope of 52.6 mV dec−1 and interfacial charge-transfer resistance of 178 Ω. Mechanism: Under working potentials, a single oxygen atom dynamically adsorbs onto the Ru1-N4 site to form an O-Ru1-N4 configuration; this adsorption induces structural relaxation (shortening of Ru-N bonds) and electronic changes (increased electron transfer from Ru 4d to N 2p and O), optimizing the binding energy of oxygen intermediates and lowering the energy barrier for the O-O coupling step (formation of OOH*), thereby enhancing activity and stability by preventing lattice oxygen evolution and Ru dissolution.. Limitations: Theoretical overpotential values are slightly higher than experimental values due to the use of simplified models in the DFT calculations. Future work: The discovery of structural evolution under working conditions provides a coordination-engineered strategy for designing high-performance acidic OER electrocatalysts for future PEMWE applications. Quote: "The single-atom Ru-N-C catalyst delivers an exceptionally intrinsic activity, reaching a mass activity as high as 3571 A gmetal−1 and turnover frequency of 3348 O2 h−1 with a low overpotential of 267 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2."
